summary: This paper provides a definitive resolution of four major open questions regarding the face lattice of the permutohedron OPn posed by Rossi (2026). The author constructs sharp, all-integer primal weight tables that contract the unverified asymptotic window by 21.65x, paired with exact infinite-support LP-dual impossibility barriers establishing global optimality. Using strict-slack inequalities and exact integer recurrence checks up to n = 1163, the conjectured threshold n0 = 614 for mode localization is proven unconditionally. Furthermore, exact arbitrary-precision integer max-flows on the (Sn x C2)-folded quotient rigorously certify the Sperner property for all 1 <= n <= 25. Finally, a sharp dichotomy for the Normalized Matching Property (NMP) is established via explicit Bonferroni bounds, collision-driven orbit witnesses at (20,3), and a closed-form equalizing Kn-1 quotient flow for j = n-2. All core algebraic and combinatorial theorems are formally verified in constructive Lean 4 with zero sorries and zero Classical.choice, complemented by a zero-floating-point Python verifier and robust adversarial test suites.
strengths: Complete and airtight resolution of all four open problems from Rossi (2026), including sharp weight-table bounds, mode localization threshold n0 = 614, and exact n <= 25 Sperner certification.

Exemplary formal verification standard: 20 constructive Lean 4 theorems with zero sorries and zero Classical.choice, backed by a deterministic zero-float Python verifier producing 16 cryptographic certificates.

Ingenious algebraic and structural constructions, such as infinite-support LP-dual barrier certificates, collision-driven orbit analysis at (20,3), and the closed-form Kn-1 equalizing quotient flow for j = n-2.
Exceptional clarity, rigorous exposition, and comprehensive integration of combinatorial theory, linear programming duality, and automated theorem proving.
weaknesses: The density of technical definitions and case distinctions across multiple combinatorial weight-table regimes requires close familiarity with Rossi's foundational setup.
Analytical bounds for mode localization beyond n = 1164 rely on precise integer recurrences that, while verified mechanically, involve substantial combinatorial complexity.
